title: Kernel confidence estimator with seqlen bucketing and prefill/decode switchboard
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Problem: Kernel choice is brittle across heterogeneous hardware and variable request seqlen distributions. We see spikey p95s when the runtime picks a high-throughput microkernel for median seqlens but that kernel exhibits high variance on longer prefixes. Goal: implement a lightweight confidence estimator that predicts per-model-per-shape kernel latency variance and combine that with explicit seqlen bucketing plus a prefill/decode switchboard to choose kernels deterministically and safely at runtime.

Scope:
- Build an offline profiling pipeline (microbenchmarks) that produces kernel latency distributions across representative token lengths, batch sizes, and quantization profiles for each supported kernel.
- Train or fit a compact confidence estimator (logistic reg / small GBDT) that maps fingerprint features (arch, sm_count, dtype, seqlen_bucket, batch_shape, cached_kv_size) to an expected latency variance and confidence score.
- Integrate estimator into the kernel selection path as a pluggable policy that can: 1) select a primary kernel when confidence >= threshold, 2) trigger a quick trial probe (1-3 requests) for marginal cases, or 3) select a conservative fallback kernel.
- Implement seqlen bucketing rules used by both prefill (where fused-attention is attractive) and decode (where single-step latency stability is critical). Buckets are ephemeral and tunable via runtime config.
- Add a prefill/decode switchboard: different policies for prefill vs decode phases (favor fused high-throughput kernels for prefill; favor low-variance single-step kernels for decode; allow controlled reuse when confidence and cached KV footprint are low).

Deliverables:
- profiling tabular artifacts (S3) and an ingestion job that populates kernel fingerprint store.
- estimator service/library and tests.
- runtime integration and feature flag guarded rollout.
- telemetry: per-route kernel selection logs, probe outcomes, regression alerts.

Success criteria (acceptance):
- p95 decode latency improves or remains stable; target: reduce decode p95 variance by 30% on workloads with mixed seqlens.
- overall token cost does not increase >2% for the same throughput.
- automated rollback if estimator-driven selection increases error rate or OOMs.

Notes: solution must be low-latency (<200ns added to hot-path) and resilient to skewed traffic (rapidly changing seqlen mix).
implementation_notes:
High-level design: offline profiler runs nightly across target GPUs (A100/V100/H100) and quantization configs. Fingerprint schema will be compact strings: model_id|arch|kernel_id|dtype|seqlen_bucket|batch_size. Estimator uses precomputed histogram moments (mean, var, 90th) as features. We will implement the estimator as a small C++/Rust artifact with a thin Python wrapper for tests and ingestion. Runtime policy: feature-flagged, rollout by route. Probe logic: allow up to 3 trial in-flight requests captured as 'probe' mode with special tags; probes use speculative batching limits to avoid perturbing normal traffic.

Trade-offs discussed:
- ML model vs heuristics: starting with a simple GBDT-like scorer allows quick iteration; pure heuristic rules are easier to reason about and will be preserved if estimator is removed.
- Probe overhead vs accuracy: we cap probe fraction to 0.1% of traffic initially, widen only if stable.
- Prefill fused kernels reduce token cost but can increase memory pressure; switchboard must evaluate cached KV footprint before reusing fused kernels during decode.

Risk mitigation: explicit circuit breaker: if >1% extra OOMs or 10% latency regressions observed in the canary group, automatically disable estimator-based selection for that route.
